title: Singapore, Michigan: The Town Buried Under the Dunes

sources.what: 'founded by Eastern investors in 1837'; 'notorious wild cat bank which printed more money than it was able to back up with gold'; forest 'had been clear-cut'; mill 'dismantled in 1875 and shipped north to St. Ignace'

marker S0191, erected 1958, Saugatuck City Hall: 'Founded in the 1830's by New York land speculators, who hoped it would rival Chicago or Milwaukee as a lake port'; the site lies beneath the sands near the mouth of the Kalamazoo River
'supplied much of the timber used to rebuild the city' after the 1871 Chicago fire

sources.who: Great Lakes Echo (MSU, 2014); SDHC site inventory

beats.text: The ruins of a town lie buried under the sand dunes of Lake Michigan.
beats.label: NEAR SAUGATUCK, MICHIGAN
beats.credit: Saugatuck-Douglas History Center; Michigan historical marker

beats.text: It was called Singapore. New York land speculators founded it in the 1830s, hoping it would rival Chicago or Milwaukee.
beats.label: FOUNDED IN THE 1830s

beats.text: After the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, its lumber helped rebuild the city.
beats.label: AFTER THE CHICAGO FIRE, 1871

beats.text: But the forests around it had been clear-cut. In 1875, the main mill was taken apart and shipped north to St. Ignace.
beats.credit: Saugatuck-Douglas History Center; CMU Clarke Historical Library

beats.text: People left. Some buildings were moved to Saugatuck. And the sand moved in.
beats.label: THE SAND MOVED IN
beats.credit: Great Lakes Echo; Saugatuck-Douglas History Center

beats.text: Legend says one man refused to leave, climbing in and out through an upstairs window until the sand reached the roof.
beats.label: THE LEGEND

beats.text: Today, a state historical marker in Saugatuck says the site of the town lies beneath the sands, near the mouth of the Kalamazoo River.
beats.label: THE STATE MARKER

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: State marker: Saugatuck City Hall, Butler Street
